captions.linkedin:
Roughly 2x the Sharpe of plain momentum. With far smaller crashes. Same data. 📊

That's the headline from Blitz, Huij & Martens (Journal of Empirical Finance, 2011) on residual momentum.

Classic Jegadeesh-Titman momentum has 2 problems. It loads on market, size, and value factor risk. And it crashes hard in 2009-style reversals. Residual momentum fixes both.

The complete logic:

🔹 REGRESS. For each stock, run a rolling 36-month Fama-French 3-factor regression on monthly returns.
🔹 RESIDUAL. Pull out the idiosyncratic return after stripping market, size, and value betas.
🔹 FORMATION. Use the last 11 months of residuals (the standard momentum window), standardized by their own volatility (information-ratio style).
🔹 RANK by the standardized residual. Long top decile, short bottom decile. Equal-weighted.
🔹 REBALANCE monthly.

Why it works: stripping factor exposures removes the unstable, crowded loadings that drive momentum crashes. What's left is the pure behavioral underreaction signal.

Blitz et al. showed standard rational momentum explanations don't account for the residual premium. It's structurally different.
